_schema.cost_per_m3_inr: approximate installed material cost, INR/m^3 (2026 estimate, high-altitude logistics premium included where noted)
_schema.cost_note: flag if cost includes remote-site transport premium
_schema.carbon_kgco2e_per_kg: embodied carbon, kg CO2-equivalent per kg of material, cradle-to-gate (A1-A3). See carbon_citation per material for source/uncertainty; several vernacular materials (rammed earth, adobe, straw-clay, VIP, SIP, radiant barrier) have no direct database entry and are order-of-magnitude ESTIMATES, flagged as such in their own citation.

_known_discrepancies: sun_dried_mud_brick_adobe and rammed_earth here use Rijal/Yoshida and Hall/Allinson values respectively; the HIAL/FHNW Ladakh report (Hall & Geissler 2022, Table 14, citing Zurcher & Frank 2018) gives materially different numbers for the same material classes (adobe k=0.13 rho=2210 cp=1000 vs our 0.75/1600/1000; rammed earth k=0.8 rho=1200 cp=1000 vs our 1.1/2000/1000). Earthen material properties vary widely with local soil composition, moisture content and compaction method, so this is a real uncertainty, not a data-entry error -- flag it in the limitations slide and consider running the optimizer/validation with both value sets to bound sensitivity.

materials.name: Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) board
materials.cost_note: does not include remote transport premium
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — EPS insulation, cradle-to-gate (A1-A3).

materials.name: Extruded Polystyrene (XPS) board
materials.cost_note: does not include remote transport premium
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — XPS insulation, cradle-to-gate (A1-A3); ICE reports XPS close to EPS despite the different blowing agent.

materials.name: Rigid Polyurethane (PUR) foam
materials.cost_note: does not include remote transport premium
materials.carbon_citation: ICE-derived PIR/PUR rigid insulation factor as tabulated in Hasan et al., 'The Role of Embodied Carbon Databases...', Sustainability 2021 (citing ICE-insulation, PIR ~3.48 kgCO2e/kg).

materials.name: Mineral wool (rock wool) batt
materials.cost_note: does not include remote transport premium
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — mineral (rock) wool, cradle-to-gate.

materials.name: Vacuum Insulation Panel (VIP)
materials.cost_note: premium high-performance option; fragile, needs protective casing
materials.citation: Alam et al., 'Vacuum Insulation Panels for building applications', Applied Energy 2011
materials.carbon_citation: ESTIMATE, not an ICE-listed material: fumed-silica core + metallized-film envelope + evacuation process. Pavel & Blagoeva / JRC and Alam et al. (Applied Energy 2011) both note VIP has a materially higher and less standardized embodied footprint than EPS/XPS; no single authoritative per-kg figure found. Treat as order-of-magnitude only, flagged the same way materials.json already flags the adobe/rammed-earth uncertainty.

materials.name: Local stone masonry (Ladakh granite/schist, dry-set)
materials.cost_note: locally sourced near Leh/Dras, transport premium minimal
materials.citation: ASHRAE Fundamentals Handbook 2021, Ch. 26, Table 1 (granite); local sourcing note per DIHAR field reports
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — natural stone (general, quarried + dressed), cradle-to-gate. Excludes long-distance haulage to site (see cost_note for the separate transport-cost premium).

materials.name: Rammed earth wall
materials.cost_note: labor-intensive but low material transport cost
materials.citation: Hall & Allinson, 'Analysis of the hygrothermal functional properties of stabilised rammed earth', Building and Environment 2009
materials.carbon_citation: Estimate for UNSTABILIZED rammed earth (no added cement), consistent with traditional Ladakhi practice: mechanical compaction energy only, no firing/calcination. If cement-stabilized (common in modern rammed earth), this can rise several-fold — cite per-project cement content if that variant is used. No ICE entry exists for rammed earth; figure follows the same order of magnitude reported for compacted-earth construction in general LCA literature (e.g. Reddy & Jagadish-style analyses of stabilized/unstabilized soil blocks).

materials.name: Sun-dried mud brick (traditional Ladakhi 'sokpa')
materials.cost_note: very low cost, locally made; used in traditional Ladakhi construction
materials.citation: Rijal & Yoshida, 'Thermal performance of traditional Ladakhi houses', Journal of Asian Architecture 2005
materials.carbon_citation: Estimate for sun-dried (unfired) mud brick: manual forming + solar drying only, no kiln. Same caveat as rammed_earth above — figure is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not an ICE-sourced number, since sun-dried earthen units aren't in the standard databases.

materials.name: Cross-Laminated Timber (CLT) panel
materials.cost_note: prefab panel, includes standard transport but not helicopter/high-altitude premium
materials.carbon_citation: Cradle-to-gate (A1-A3), EXCLUDING biogenic carbon storage. ICE v4.1 gives softwood lumber ~0.31 kgCO2e/kg for the fossil energy of felling/sawing/kiln-drying; CLT's adhesive bonding + additional processing pushes typical manufacturer EPDs to ~0.4-0.5. The wood itself also STORES roughly 1.6 kgCO2e/kg of biogenic carbon absorbed during growth — real, but declared separately under EN 15804+A2 rather than netted off here, because it's released again if the timber is later burned or left to decompose.

materials.name: Structural Insulated Panel (SIP, EPS core + OSB skins)
materials.cost_note: effective composite value; prefab, modular, fast to erect
materials.citation: SIPA (Structural Insulated Panel Association) Technical Bulletin, effective U-value data; ASHRAE 2021 for core k
materials.carbon_citation: ESTIMATE: mass-weighted composite of OSB skins (~0.45-0.5 kgCO2e/kg, wood panel + resin) and EPS core (3.29 kgCO2e/kg, see expanded_polystyrene_eps), using the OSB skins' much higher density to weight their mass share despite the core's larger volume fraction. No single EPD covers this exact composite; treat as a rough figure, same 'effective composite value' caveat as the existing cost/k entries for this material.

materials.name: Galvanized steel structural frame
materials.cost_note: priced as structural framing member volume, not cladding
materials.carbon_citation: ICE v4.1 general structural steel (~1.55 kgCO2e/kg, av. recycled content) plus an estimated +0.08 kgCO2e/kg for hot-dip galvanizing (zinc coating). Recycled-content steel can be materially lower (ICE gives ~0.45 for high-recycled steel) — this figure assumes ordinary/average recycled content, not a verified-recycled supply chain.

materials.name: Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (AAC) block
materials.cost_note: does not include remote transport premium; blocks are bulky/fragile for helicopter transport
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — aerated concrete block, cradle-to-gate (as tabulated in the public ICE summary; reference product rho ~750 kg/m3 vs. this entry's 550 kg/m3, so treat as same-category, not an exact density match).

materials.name: Double-glazed Low-E window unit
materials.cost_note: priced per m^2 of glazing area (standard practice), not per m^3; U-value ~1.1-1.4 W/m2K typical
materials.citation: ASHRAE Fundamentals Handbook 2021, Ch. 15; ISO 10077-1 for U-value convention
materials.carbon_citation: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon & Energy (ICE) Database v3.0, University of Bath / Circular Ecology, 2019 — float glass, cradle-to-gate, applied to the glazing layer's mass only. Frame, spacer, Low-E coating and gas fill are NOT separately counted (consistent with cost_per_m2_inr, which also prices glazing area only, not the frame) — treat as a glass-only lower bound, not the full window-unit footprint.

materials.name: Triple-glazed, krypton-filled, Low-E window unit
materials.cost_note: priced per m^2; premium cold-climate glazing, U-value ~0.6-0.8 W/m2K
materials.citation: Passive House Institute component database; ISO 10077-1
materials.carbon_citation: Same float-glass basis as double_glazed_low_e_window (see that entry's citation) applied to this unit's (higher, 3-pane) glass mass. The krypton gas fill has a disproportionately high specific production footprint but a tiny mass share per unit; no reliable per-kg figure for krypton fill was found, so it is EXCLUDED here — this is a glass-only figure, likely a modest underestimate for this specific product.

materials.name: Straw-clay block (100x25cm, cylindrical cavities)
materials.cost_note: no INR cost data available; used in HIAL Ladakh passive solar houses
materials.citation: Hall & Geissler (FHNW), 'Thermal comfort in Passive Solar Houses in Ladakh' (2022), Table 14, citing Zurcher & Frank, Building Physics, 5th ed. 2018
materials.carbon_citation: Estimate: raw straw + clay/soil binder, hand-formed, no firing — same order of magnitude as sun-dried adobe (see that entry), and for the same reason (no database entry exists for straw-clay construction specifically). Some LCA studies count straw's biogenic carbon and report straw-clay as net-negative; this figure does NOT include that credit, consistent with how cross_laminated_timber_clt's biogenic storage is also kept separate above.

materials.name: Reflective foil radiant barrier (roof underlay)
materials.cost_note: priced per m^2 as thin membrane; effective emissivity ~0.05, reduces radiant heat loss to sky
materials.citation: ASTM C1224; manufacturer datasheets (typical foil-faced polyethylene bubble insulation)
materials.carbon_citation: ESTIMATE: thin primary-aluminium foil layer (ICE v4.1 primary aluminium ~13.1 kgCO2e/kg, but a small mass fraction of this laminated product) bonded to a plastic film/foam backing (~2 kgCO2e/kg range for generic PE film). No product-specific EPD was found; treat as a rough blended figure, not a verified number.

_carbon_data_note: Added post-Phase-3 to fill the gap flagged since Phase 3 in README.md ('carbon_kgco2e is a real gap ... someone needs to source per-material embodied-carbon numbers with citations before this objective can exist for real'). Primary source is the ICE Database v3.0/v4.1 (Hammond & Jones, University of Bath / Circular Ecology) for conventional/industrial materials. Vernacular/traditional materials (rammed earth, sun-dried adobe, straw-clay) and a few composites (VIP, SIP, radiant barrier) have NO entry in ICE or comparable databases, so their figures are order-of-magnitude estimates flagged individually — same honesty standard as the existing adobe/rammed-earth k/rho/cp _known_discrepancies note below. These numbers are now wired into engine/optimizer/objectives.py as a REPORTED figure (shown to the user, used to pick a 'Lowest Carbon' curated design) but are deliberately NOT added to the NSGA-II search objective vector this pass — folding a 4th axis into the optimizer's domination/surrogate logic is a bigger, riskier change than reporting a real number on an already-existing front, and given the estimate-heavy entries above, treating carbon as an authoritative search target this early would overstate how solid this data is. Worth revisiting once the estimate-flagged entries have better sources.
